question.problem:
Find the Cartesian equation for the line with the following vector equation:

$$
r=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -6 \\ 13\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$
question.worked_solution:
Using the usual formula, we get

$$
\frac{x-1}{-2}=\frac{y-(-6)}{5}=\frac{z-13}{0}=t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),
$$

or equivalently

$$
\frac{x-1}{-2}=\frac{y+6}{5}=\frac{z-13}{0},
$$

which is problematic because $\frac{z-13}{0}$ involves division by zero.

However, notice that in our line, the $z$ component always maintains the constant value of $z=13:$

$$
r=[\begin{aligned}1-2t \\ -6+5t \\ 13\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$

So, in the Cartesian equation, we remove the $\frac{z-13}{0}$ part and instead write $z=13$, as follows:

$$
\frac{x-1}{-2}=\frac{y+6}{5},\,z=13
$$
